description: What InternetData knows about one autonomous system, by its number: its operator, country, registry, allocation date and domain, the kind of network it runs, how many IPv4 addresses and prefixes it announces with their RPKI counts, its ASN Whois record, its rank and whether it is Tier 1, the AS numbers it gets transit from, peers with and provides transit to, how many domains it hosts with the most popular, and the prefixes it announces in global BGP with their RPKI status. The prefixes and each list of AS numbers hold their first 100, the AS numbers ascending, with `truncated` giving the total where there are more. An AS no database knows comes back as its number with empty values. Always read `coverage.note` before concluding anything from a field that is not in the result.
name: lookup_asn

coverage.description: Which datasets this result covered. Read `note` before interpreting any absent field.

result.description: What every database says about one AS.

cap_reached.description: On every answer to a key on a paid plan, and on no other: `false` while the answer has every field, `true` once its organization's overage cap is reached and the answer has the core fields. Lookups answered past the cap are not billed; raising or removing the cap in Billing turns it `false` again.

country.description: The country its registry assigned it to.

downstreams.description: Those AS numbers, ascending, up to 20000. On a paid plan or a free key's full answers.

hosted_domains.description: From ASN Hosted Domains: how many registered domains the AS hosts, and the 10 most popular. Its database lists up to 1,000 an AS. On a paid plan or a free key's full answers.

domains.description: Up to 10 of them, the most popular first; `[]` when none does.

total.description: How many registered domains resolve to an address the AS announces.

num_downstreams.description: How many AS numbers it provides transit to. On a paid plan or a free key's full answers.

num_ips.description: IPv4 addresses it announces. On a paid plan or a free key's full answers.

num_peers.description: How many AS numbers it exchanges its own and its customers' routes with. On a paid plan or a free key's full answers.

num_prefixes4.description: IPv4 prefixes it announces. On a paid plan or a free key's full answers.

num_prefixes6.description: IPv6 prefixes it announces. On a paid plan or a free key's full answers.

num_upstreams.description: How many AS numbers it gets transit from. On a paid plan or a free key's full answers.

peers.description: Those AS numbers, ascending, up to 20000. On a paid plan or a free key's full answers.

prefixes.description: What it announces, IPv4 then IPv6, up to 20000 a family. On a paid plan or a free key's full answers.

first_seen.description: The first day BGP Route saw it.

size.description: IPv4 addresses it covers; 0 for IPv6.

rank.description: Its rank in ASN Extended, by customer cone, 1 the largest; `0` for an AS seen in no AS path. On a paid plan or a free key's full answers.

rpki_invalid.description: Invalid. On a paid plan or a free key's full answers.

rpki_not_found.description: With no RPKI record. On a paid plan or a free key's full answers.

rpki_valid.description: Its announcements RPKI calls valid. On a paid plan or a free key's full answers.

tier1.description: Whether it is one of the transit-free networks at the top of the hierarchy, which get transit from no one and peer with each other. On a paid plan or a free key's full answers.

trial_expired.description: On every answer to a key on the free plan, and on no other: `false` while its organization's lookups of the UTC day answer every field, `true` once those are used up and the answer has the core fields.

type.description: The kind of network it runs. On a paid plan or a free key's full answers.

upstreams.description: Those AS numbers, ascending, up to 20000. On a paid plan or a free key's full answers.

whois.description: Its ASN Whois record, every column, empty where the registry states nothing. On a paid plan or a free key's full answers.

truncated.description: Present only when the answer was cut short: for each list it cut, how many entries it carries and how many there are, and where to get them all.

title: Look up an AS
